Changelog

From build 5 the releases carry build numbers, not versions: build 5 follows 0.04, the next is build 6.

Build 22 (2026-10-25): a restore is never disturbed

  • While a session is being restored over USB, saving or loading a session on the FM-1 shows BUSY. A restore keeps its sectors reserved and half a sector waiting between its messages; a save or a load in the middle of it shares the same buffer and could take the same sectors. Found by the first restore on the device, which stopped with "the flash failed" (the session there kept, as it should be); six restores after it went through. A restore abandoned half-way frees them 5 s after its last message. Test: host backup.
  • tools/fm1_sessions.py restore says which step failed, if one does.

Build 21 (2026-10-25): sessions restored over USB

  • Sessions can be written back to the FM-1 over USB (Tonitor's backup protocol, now with its writes): the website's backup page and tools/fm1_sessions.py restore FILE put a saved session back in its slot, replacing the one there only once the new copy is whole and checked. Only blank sectors or Norilsk's own retired ones are written — never another firmware's. A damaged record is refused and the session already there kept. Test: host backup.
  • tools/fm1_sessions.py talks only to an FM-1 whose USB name is FM-1 Norilsk (Tonitor and Bigorna answer the same identity).

Build 20 (2026-10-25): PLAY is the loops'

  • PLAY is for the loops only. With an effect slot chosen it does nothing — pressed, held, with SHIFT — and stays dark (before, it worked the loops of the generator chosen last). With a generator chosen, its light glows dimly when the generator has loops, lit while they play, dark when it has none. Muting stays where it was: a slot button held 0.8 s. Test: host looper.
  • Both kinds of mute are in a snapshot: each slot's (build 18) and each loop's held out or in (build 19, host whole).

Build 19 (2026-10-25): a snapshot is the whole machine

  • A snapshot holds the whole machine now: besides every slot (sounds, effects, values, cables, levels, pans, mutes, sends), the master delay and reverb, the modulation, the scale and the DISINTEGRATOR, also how it is played — each generator's latched notes, whether its loops play, which are held out, their direction, speed, VARY and moves along the scale — and the octave and the draw's path. Recalled, the notes latched since are let go and the snapshot's are held again, the loops start or stop as stored; by a morph, that happens at its middle. The loops' recordings themselves are the session's (each looper is 4.5 KiB: sixteen copies would not fit the RAM): a snapshot says how they play, not what they hold. The morph time and the slot chosen are not in it (how you move between snapshots, where you look). Sessions are format 3; formats 1 and 2 are read (their snapshots leave how it is played as it is). Test: host whole.
  • A morph's end refreshes its clouds: a CLOUD swapped in during a morph, frozen, held what the generators made while still crossing over. At the end it takes the sound again, its grains going on over it.
  • The black keys belong to the view: the loops' REVERSE, PENDULUM, RANDOM, HALF, DOUBLE (4th .. 8th) work only while PLAY is held, where they glow dimly and the ones on are lit (Tonitor's). Playing, those keys do nothing and stay dark, kept for what comes later.
  • DISINTEGRATOR on one line: a font of its own (28 pt, its letters only), as large as the word fits the screen.
  • SHIFT + the 1st black key says RAND PARAMS.

Build 18 (2026-10-25): Norilsk

  • The firmware is now Norilsk (Molecular until build 17). The screen at power-on, the USB name ("FM-1 Norilsk", a product number of its own, 0x0008, so a computer shows the new name), the package (build/norilsk.fwsc), the sources. Its sessions stay: the same flash area, the same records.
  • SAVE and SHIFT + SAVE swapped: SAVE brings up the SNAPSHOTS page (SAVE again: back); SHIFT + SAVE the SESSIONS page. SAVE held while playing still saves the session; on the SNAPSHOTS page it stores into the snapshot framed. A white key held 0.8 s on the SNAPSHOTS page stores into its snapshot (as before).
  • KNOB 1: the DISINTEGRATOR of the generator the keys play, 0 .. 100, on a large dial in its colour (KNOB 1 is the morph time only on the SNAPSHOTS page now). An unstable gate on the generator's sound, before its cables, so the effects hear it too: the sound goes as a chain of pulses of uneven length; a pulse lets it through, gates it down (to nothing from 60 up), stutters a slice of what it just made (10 .. 90 ms, repeated), or crushes it (bits and rate), and may throw its dry part across the stereo image. The higher, the shorter and less even the pulses, the more of them act, the deeper and wider. Every edge glides (~1.5 ms). Ideas from Destroy FX's Skidder and from buffer repeaters, none of their code. Kept with snapshots and sessions, glided by a morph. Test: host dis.
  • Two draw paths (toggles, lit while on, one at a time, kept with the session): the 2nd black key ABRASIVE — the harsh scenes and families (BRUIT, SHATTER, FURNACE, STATIC, SCRAPE, DATA, METAL), more cables and cross-modulation, the torn and crushed recipes, the effects' values driven; the 3rd black key DARK — the FIELD scene, drones, hums, tunnels, ash, freezes, nothing harsh, 3 dB quieter, the spaces and ringing recipes (SPACE, GHOST, ABYSS, FREEZER, RESONANT ..), the values darker and less driven. Neither: anything goes, every draw as before. The engine draws each sound as ever (the golden hashes unchanged). Test: host paths.
  • SHIFT + the 1st black key: the chosen effect slot's every value drawn anew (the path's way), in place — no break, its effects and cables stay; on a generator, a new sound of its family, its cables kept. Test: host revalue.
  • Eight modulation slots a slot (four before): MOD A .. H on the MOD page; SHIFT + SEQ throws two to six. Sessions are now format 2; a session saved before (format 1) is read, its four slots as A .. D. Test: host format1 (a session saved by build 17, tests/sessions/format1.bin).

Build 17 (2026-10-25): the hiss that a morph carried over

  • Found with session 2: snapshots 2 and 3 hold the same effects in slots 4 and 5, other cables. Recalled at once, a slot whose cables change is cleared and started again; morphed, its cables change in place and its effects go on. In snapshot 2 generator 1 feeds slot 4 (on the left): its TAPE ran. In snapshot 3 nothing reaches it — but TAPE's hiss was made whatever came in, and an effect nothing reaches runs on while it still sounds: its own hiss kept it sounding, for ever. Hence the hiss on the left in snapshot 3, after a morph only.
  • TAPE: the hiss is under what passes (the input and the echoes), ~0.3 s out after them, and gone with them.
  • Every effect falls silent with nothing in (or fades, as a long echo does; a frozen CLOUD holds, as it should). Others held a sound of their own for ever: BANK and MODAL a tone from their resonators' last digit raised x 600 (the resonator now works 256 times finer), STARVE a level (its lean filter stopped short of the lean), FILTER at a high Q a small remainder (let go when nothing comes in). The level meter of each effect stopped at 15 instead of 0, and an effect under 32 (-60 dB, was 8) for 2 s with nothing in now rests. Test: host quiet (each effect, four ways: fed 1 s, then 40 s of nothing).

Build 16 (2026-10-25): a recall is never left half done

  • A snapshot recalled while a slot is still taking the last change (its fade and clearing, ~15 ms; or a voice still on the sound about to be replaced) used to show BUSY and stop there: the slots that had not taken it kept the snapshot before, sounding inside the new one. Now the rest is given in the frames that follow, until every part has it (10 s at most). The same at a morph's end: after its 3 s of grace it went on as if done; now it keeps going until it is. Test: host recall (twelve cases; all twelve failed before).
  • A snapshot stored by build 14 held stale cable places past a generator's last, so every recall took the generator for changed and started its notes again (a break in the sound for nothing). They are ignored now.
  • Found with session 2 copied from the FM-1 (build 15): host replay of its 3 -> 2 -> 3 at morph times 0 .. 30 s, back at once or while on its way, lands on snapshot 3 within 3 dB, each side and each band. Session 2 was saved with MORPH OFF and a note latched only on generator 1.

Build 15 (2026-10-25): the sessions read over USB

  • The sessions can be copied to the computer, to find what the morph leaves behind in session 2: Tonitor's backup protocol, reading only (backup.c: 0x50 the list, 0x51 a piece of a record; the writes are refused, nothing is written to the flash). tools/fm1_sessions.py lists the sessions and saves one (save 2: build/session_2.bin); build/host replay build/session_2.bin 3 2 plays it on the computer: snapshot 3, a morph to 2 and back, against 3 recalled at once (each side's and each generator's loudness; WAVs in build/). Test: host backup.
  • Nothing else changes.

Build 14 (2026-10-25): the morph fixed; its dial; the snapshots' keys

  • A morph no longer carries the snapshot before into the one after. An effect slot whose effects stayed the same had its values glided in place, its memory kept: a frozen CLOUD went on holding the earlier snapshot's sound for ever (recalled at once, the slot was cleared — and a frozen CLOUD then stayed empty and silent). Now a slot with a CLOUD whose values change is swapped (faded out, cleared, faded in) like a slot whose effects change, and a fresh CLOUD fills its 0.74 s with the sound playing before it freezes. Tests: host ends (twelve morphs, each against the same snapshot applied at once to a fresh machine: the same state, the same loudness), host hiss (a hissing TAPE morphed into a quiet one).
  • KNOB 1's dial: turned, on the playing page or the SNAPSHOTS page, it covers the screen for 1.5 s — MORPH, the time very large (4.5, or OFF), SECONDS, a bar of its reach (0 .. 30 s). (The large font gained . O S.)
  • The SNAPSHOTS page's keys: every stored snapshot's key glows dimly, the one chosen lit, the one a morph flows into blinking.

Build 13 (2026-10-25): snapshots morph

  • KNOB 1 (playing, and on the SNAPSHOTS page) sets the morph time, 0 .. 30 s in half seconds (MORPH 4.5 S; 0: OFF, at once as before); kept with the session.
  • A snapshot recalled with a morph time flows into place: every level (finer than its 1.5 dB steps while it glides; mutes faded through it), pan and send, the master reverb's DECAY DAMP MIX and the delay's FEEDBACK DAMP MIX, the LFOs' rates, fades and amounts, and an effect slot's values where the same effects stand in the same places, glided all the way. A generator whose sound changes: its held and latched notes cross over, the old sound fading out on its voice while the new one comes in on a voice of its own; an effect slot whose effects change: faded out, changed, faded back in — each its own stretch of the morph, generators and slots taking turns (the voices and the memory allow one at a time). At the middle what has no between: the scale and root, the LFOs' shapes and courses, cables where nothing else changes, the reverb's SIZE and the delay's TIME (glided, they would bend the pitch). At the end the snapshot exactly as stored. Recalled again on the way: a new morph from where it is.
  • The snapshot it flows into blinks on the SNAPSHOTS page, and its key, until it is there.
  • A test, host morph: notes held through a 4 s morph between snapshots apart in nearly everything — never silent, old and new sounds heard together, levels gliding in steps of a few 256ths, SIZE kept to the middle, the snapshot exactly at the end.

Build 12 (2026-10-25): the dull effects made drastic

Saved sessions and snapshots that use these effects sound different from build 12 on (their values are kept; what they do with them changed).

  • FILTER: a notch beside low-, band- and high-pass; DRIVE (x 1 .. x 12, tanh) into it in place of the slow drift (with more resonance it would have swept like a siren); RES up to Q 12, squelchy and screechy but kept off the eardrums — its level comes down as the resonance goes up, the resonance is pulled back above 3 kHz, a soft ceiling under full scale. A test, host ears: every type at its highest resonance, across its range: at most 0.44 of full scale and +2.7 dB over the dry.
  • MULAW: down to 2 bits (was 4), rates down to FS / 32 (1.4 kHz; was FS / 8), the filters open far enough to alias, drive up to x 8.
  • SHIFT: shifts of 40 .. 900 Hz (every partial moved off the harmonics; small shifts sounded like a chorus); the feedback gone (fed back, a shifter spirals: a barber pole) for DRIVE into it (denser sidebands); TONE after it.
  • MODAL: its modes further apart (up to 4.2 times), the sound driven into them, their ring brought up with the Q under a soft ceiling: from -14 dB against the dry to +5.
  • VOWEL: formants three times sharper (Q 10 .. 60), driven harder (x 2 .. x 16), brought up with the Q.
  • TAPE: DROPOUTS in place of the wow (the echoes gone 20 .. 200 ms, up to twice a second; the time's own wander a breath of 0.1 %); AGE now saturates the head harder, darkens to 3 kHz and adds hiss.

Build 11 (2026-10-25): rewiring; six drastic effects

  • The first black key rewires the chosen slot: a generator's cables into the effect slots and its modulation by another generator drawn anew (HOME's rules), its sound, send and levels as they are — taken without a fade, the notes going on; an effect slot's outs to the master and cables across to the slots after it drawn anew, its effects and values as they are, changed in place (no fade, nothing cleared). The top band says REWIRED and the slot.
  • Six new effects, more drastic, after open sources (ideas, not code): CLOUD (a granular freezer, after Mutable Instruments' Clouds and Beads: SIZE, DENSITY, FREEZE, SPREAD; frozen above the middle of FREEZE), SCREAM (a saturated feedback network, a no-input mixer's howl, ducked by the input so it dies with it: SIZE, FEEDBACK, TONE, DRIVE), RING (a diode ring modulator after Parker's model, a fixed carrier or the sound's own past: FREQ, DIODE, SELF, TONE), STARVE (a starved, gated fuzz after the Fuzz Factory: it sputters and tears: GAIN, GATE, BIAS, TONE), CHEB (a Chebyshev re-voicer after Airwindows' Pafnuty: SHAPE, ODD, DRIVE, TONE), BANK (an inharmonic resonator bank after Rings and Elements — a bar, a plate, a bell, a membrane: PITCH, Q, SET, BRIGHT). None bends a pitch; none rings on by itself (host fxtails).
  • Six new recipes: FREEZER, FEEDBACK, FOUNDRY, GONG, SPECTRE, SPUTTER; HELL, FACTORY and ABYSS may draw the new effects too.
  • A test, host rewire: the sound byte for byte the same, no note cut, the cables new every time.

Build 10 (2026-10-25): invisible hands, grit, new families and recipes

Engine generation 3 (dsp.h GEN_NOW 3). Generations 0 .. 2 draw and sound as before, bit for bit (tests/golden).

  • The invisible hand (Anima's, Tonitor's anima.c after Vascular's AnimaCore.h), a hand on each voice: one finger on the sound dragging figures (orbits, figures of eight, scribbles, slow glides, now and then a flick), pressing in slow swells, landing elsewhere every ~18 s; a ghost finger on a clock that will not keep time. Each sound's design maps the hand's controllers (where it is, how hard it presses, how fast it moves, its angle, distance, age; the whole hand; how many fingers) to two to four of: the modulators' brightness (never the carriers' level), the cloud, the level (a harder press never quieter), the grit, the glitches, the cloud's darkness. Never the pitch. 85 % of the sounds of generation 3 have one; AMBIENT's slower, EXPERIMENTAL's quicker.
  • Grit (Russolo's, Tonitor's russolo.c after Robert Heel's Noisferatu), after the operators: a small DAC (bits kept, the sample held), bitwise logic (the sound XOR'd with a triangle at a ratio to the note, as loud as the sound), stutters (the moment just before looped a few rounds, from the voice's own buffer), and bent grains (the cloud read with an address bit flipped). The older families on EXPERIMENTAL get a little of it now and then.
  • Eight new families: FURNACE (a low roaring feedback body, crushed, under a dark cloud), HUM (carriers nailed near 50 and 100 Hz, beating, XOR'd: a machine room), STATIC (noise from feedback, crushed hard, stuttering, shattered and bent), HOWL (formants an octave down under long dark grains), SCRAPE (high inharmonic metal, bent grains, held samples), DATA (glass through bitwise logic, crushed, stuttering pulsars), ASH (a dark drone under a sparse dusty crackle), TUNNEL (one or two octaves down, a huge dark fed-back cloud, sometimes frozen). All held and moving (generation 2's rules after them; host sustain: 1200 sounds, none struck, none fading).
  • A new effect, GLITCH (Russolo's bent buffers): the sound through a 0.74 s line read at its own speed (never another pitch), its address bent, jumped, or stuttering on a clock; changes cross-faded. Values BEND, CLOCK, STUTTER, SPAN. Tile GLT.
  • Six new recipes: HELL (torn, rung, a vast room), FACTORY (crushed, metal resonance, echoes), GLITCH (bent buffers, reversed or crushed), BROADCAST (a broken transmission), ABYSS (moved partials ringing, deep), RUST (a spring, torn, glitched).
  • Fixed for generation 3: a grain read backwards no longer reaches into an earlier note's leftovers in its buffer (an old flaw, kept as it was for generations 0 .. 2); a voice let go and silent a quarter second ends.
  • Memory: each effect slot 47 KiB (the largest recipe drawn needs 46.5); the build prints what is truly free in the pool after CPU1's stacks (9.2 KiB).

Build 9 (2026-10-25): pages paint in one pass

  • Every page used to be painted twice on the way in: the whole screen filled with black first (Tonitor never does), then the page — two sweeps down the screen at 12 MHz, ~77 ms each, seen as the page unfurling. Now each page paints every one of its pixels itself and nothing else: one pass, as Tonitor's. Back on the playing page only the gaps between its parts are painted, an effect row blanks only between its tiles, and a whole redraw (or a row that changed) draws its tiles in the same frame.
  • A new test, host paint: every page entered over a flood of a colour no page uses — none left, and exactly one screen of pixels sent; a slot drawn anew 24 times under the playing page, the screen the same as a whole repaint.

Build 8 (2026-10-25): sessions, snapshots, LFOs

  • Sessions (Tonitor's, sessions.c): SAVE opens the SESSIONS page — PRESETS through 64 slots (the number very large: red holding a session, grey empty), SAVE loads one, or starts a new session in an empty one; SAVE held 0.8 s saves into the session loaded or chosen (on the page: into the slot shown, asked SAVE NEW / OVERWRITE?, NO / YES on PRESETS). A session keeps every generator (its sound as what draws it again, bit for bit, and its measured level; its cables, modulation by another, level, pan, mute, sends), every effect slot (its patch whole), the master delay and reverb, the six slots' LFOs, the scale, root, octave, slot chosen, the loops' moves, every looper's loops, the latched notes, and its snapshots. The whole screen says SAVED / LOADED / NEW and the number.
  • Snapshots (Bigorna's patterns, renamed): SHIFT + SAVE opens the SNAPSHOTS page, 16 a session in four rows. A white key let go soon recalls its snapshot; held 0.8 s stores the state now in it; SHIFT and held empties it. PRESETS moves the frame, SAVE recalls the one framed, SAVE held stores into it. A snapshot is the machine's state but the loops, the latched notes, the octave and the slot chosen. Kept with the session when it is saved.
  • The flash: Tonitor's record format and its order of writing (the new copy first, then the old one retired), in the area Tonitor and Bigorna use (0x97000 .. 0xE0000). Unlike them, Molecular writes only into blank sectors and its own retired records, and never erases another firmware's data. Two fixes on Tonitor's scheme: a retired record's later sectors are looked at one by one (a sector blanked and reused since is not lost), and of two copies of a session the newer stays only if its body checks (a power cut while it was written keeps the older).
  • LFOs (Tonitor's modulation, mod.c): SEQ's third page, MOD, for the slot chosen — two LFOs (SHAPE, RATE, MODE, FADE) and four slots (FROM, TO, AMOUNT; NOW shows what it does). A generator's destinations: its four macros, level, pan, reverb and delay sends, the LFOs' rates. An effect slot's: the values of the effects standing in it, by place (named on the page by the effect there now: a slot drawn anew, the LFO moves the new effect's value at that place), its level and pan, the rates. SHIFT + SEQ throws the chosen slot's modulation anew. Nothing is modulated until set.
  • Tests: host sessions (another firmware's sectors untouched through saves, overwrites, blanking and filling up; a full round trip after a restart; snapshots; power cuts; a damaged record refused), host mod.
  • Memory: RAM 75 of 96 KiB (the snapshots 5.8 KiB, a sector's buffer 4 KiB); pool unchanged.

Build 7 (2026-10-24): the master delay and reverb

  • Tonitor's master delay and reverb (master.c), at the end of the chain, after the three effect slots. They hear what the mix holds: each generator's dry share, after its level, at its sends; and each effect slot's output at the mean send of the generators wired into it. The delay first (mono; its echoes to both sides, half of them into the reverb), then the plate (mono in, stereo out). Their returns follow the owner's rule: 2 s after the last voice (no loop going round) they fade out in 0.5 s.
  • KNOB 3: the delay send of the generator the keys play; KNOB 4: its reverb send (0 .. 100; Tonitor's KNOB 4 and SHIFT + KNOB 4). At power-on every reverb send 40, every delay send 0.
  • SEQ: the DELAY page (TIME 20 ms .. 2 s, FEEDBACK, DAMP, MIX), again the REVERB page (SIZE, DECAY, DAMP, MIX), again back; KNOB 1 .. 4 set the four rows. Tonitor's defaults and pages.
  • Differences from Tonitor: a change of the delay's TIME cross-fades instead of gliding (no bend of pitch); the plate's SIZE goes to 1.0, not 1.25 (memory).
  • Memory: the delay's 2 s line (44 100 B) in the pool, paid by each effect slot's memory, 60 KiB to 50 KiB (the largest recipe drawn needs 43 KiB; a slot no longer holds its own reverb with a delay or tape beside it); the master plate (34 KiB) in RAM (RAM 63 of 96 KiB).
  • A new test, host master: sends at 0 add nothing (bit for bit); each send is heard; a generator heard only through an effect slot reaches the master through the slot.

Build 6 (2026-10-24): the looper; nothing lingers

  • Nothing sounds on once no note is held or latched (the owner's rule). A voice let go sounds as it will for 1 s, then fades 60 dB in 2 s and ends (it could ring up to 30 s). The effect slots close, over 0.5 s, 2 s after the last voice has ended and while no loop goes round; a note opens them at once. Measured through the mixer on 24 patches: silence (under -60 dB FS) at most 5.5 s after the last key. A new test, host tails.
  • Effects that rang on by themselves, fixed: MODAL, VOWEL, SPRING (the resonator now carries the fraction each result drops into the next: a truncated high-Q resonator rang on as a tone or a DC level — MODAL up to -10 dB FS of DC); STRING and SHIFT (their loops round towards zero, so they die out). Every effect slot's output goes through a DC blocker (~8 Hz). A new test, host fxtails: every effect, 24 draws each, silent 10 s after its input.
  • The looper, Tonitor's (loop.c), one a generator, on the generator the keys play: up to ten free loops each (no tempo, no grid; each overdub its own length), about 500 notes a generator. REC arms, the first note starts, REC ends (a note still held is tied over the end: a drone stays one note), REC again overdubs; REC held 1 s empties; SHIFT + REC: VARY. PLAY stops or starts; PLAY held: the loops on the white keys (and the screen), each in or out; SHIFT + PLAY: every generator's loops. The 4th to 8th black keys: REVERSE, PENDULUM, RANDOM, HALF and DOUBLE speed. SHIFT + OCT: every loop a step of the scale (a generator's button held too: its loops only; held with SHIFT, a button no longer mutes). The keys' and the loops' notes never end each other's. A test, host looper.
  • The screen: in a generator's block, at the left, a white disc while its looper records, a ring blinking while armed, a ring while its loops play. PLAY held: the LOOPS page (Tonitor's), a numbered box a loop, in its generator's colour when in, a grey frame when out. REC and PLAY light as on Tonitor.

Build 5 (2026-10-24): textures and drones only

The owner's direction: Molecular is for evolving soundscapes. Nothing struck, plucked or pulsed; nothing that needs a sequence to make sense.

  • Generation 2 of the generators (dsp.h GEN_NOW 2; mol.c mo_gen2), applied over every family's body, the path and the mutations: the carriers swell in (no strike: they rise to the level they hold, never fall back to it) and hold high; the modulators get slow envelopes of their own, so the timbre opens and closes over many seconds; the LFO breathes (roughly 0.1 to 1 Hz) on the modulators' depth and a little on the carriers' level, never more than a trace on the pitch; no pitch envelope; the carriers detuned apart to beat; a cloud fades in. IMPACT and PULSE are no longer drawn; FREEZE and the other clouds borrow a body that holds. Generations 0 and 1 draw as before (tests/golden).
  • A new test (host sustain): 720 sounds held 10 s; each must swell in (its first quarter second at most twice what it holds), hold (its last 2 s at least a fifth of its loudest moment), and no more than 2 % may barely move. At build 5: no failures, 6 barely moving.
  • SELECT and ALGORITHM: the level and pan of the generator chosen, or chosen last while an effect slot is chosen, as on Tonitor. The effect slots' level and pan are no longer on the knobs (they stay as drawn at power-on).
  • Pans at power-on: generator 1 in the middle, 2 left, 3 right (70 % of the way). HOME no longer draws a generator's level and pan: they are the player's.
  • The startup screen says BUILD 5; the build prints build 5 in its package line.

0.04 (2026-10-24): three generators, three effect slots, two cores

The owner's design after trying 0.03: the engine is dear, so three generators instead of six.

  • The top row: FX SEL ENV are the generator slots 1 to 3, LFO EDIT GLO the effect slots 4 to 6. A press chooses the slot; a 0.8 s hold mutes it, or lets it be heard again. Nothing is switched off: a muted generator's notes go on, silent; a muted effect slot is skipped.
  • Effect slots: each a chain of two or three effects drawn from a recipe (SPACE, ECHO, METAL, STRINGS, EROSION, GHOST, SPECTRAL, RESONANT, FOLDS, TELEPHONE). HOME on an effect slot draws its recipe, its effects, their values and its cables across to the slots after it; SHIFT + HOME keeps the recipe. The same effect may stand in several slots: each is an instance in its slot's own memory (60 KiB a slot; a recipe is drawn to fit). A new patch fades the slot out, clears its memory a piece a block, and starts the new effects. REV (the plate reverb, capped at SIZE 1.0 for the memory) and DLY (the delay, now 1 s) are effects like any other.
  • Generators: HOME draws the chosen generator's sound, the effects it is wired into (one to three, in any slot, mostly at the head of a chain), its modulation by another generator, its level and pan. SHIFT + HOME keeps the family. HOME held 0.8 s draws all six slots anew.
  • Four voices for the three generators; the keys play the generator chosen last, also while an effect slot is chosen. SELECT and ALGORITHM set the chosen slot's level and pan, generator or effect slot.
  • Latching, the other way round: hold a white key and press SHIFT to latch it; hold SHIFT and press the lit key to let it go.
  • The second core (Tonitor's): CPU1 runs the effects, on what the generators sent the block before (0.73 ms later), and the voices dealt to it by their cost; CPU0 the rest. One core and two give the same sound, bit for bit (a host test). A CPU1 fault retires it until power-off, said on the screen.
  • The screen: the three generators as large numbered blocks (filled when heard, an outline when muted, framed in white when chosen, in grey when the keys play it while an effect slot is chosen); the three effect slots as rows of named tiles, each bordered in the colours of the generators wired into it, the keyboard generator's tiles filled with its colour, a muted row dark, the chosen row framed in white. No cables.
  • Effects' values are drawn within bounds that keep each one heard; SPRING takes the sound itself as well as its colour; FILTER's band-pass is kept broad.

0.03 (2026-10-23): two dice, generators and pedalboard

The owner's model: synthesizers sharing a pedalboard.

  • HOME rolls the chosen slot: its sound, the modules it is wired into (one to three, often shared with other slots), how much it sends them, its dry share, its level and pan, and now and then its modulation by another slot.
  • SAVE rolls the rack: every module's values, and how the modules are wired to each other — an order the sound runs through, from each module one or two cables to modules later in that order and/or out to the master. The slots' wiring into the rack is kept. (SEQ does nothing now.)
  • DELAY (Tonitor's) is a module again, in FLANGE's place; delay and reverb are modules like any other, no sends.
  • Nothing in the rack bends a pitch: SHIFT's shift is fixed while it sounds (its fourth value is now its feedback's tone), REVERSE plays at the sound's own pitch (no octave head; its third value is now feedback, its fourth how far back it reaches), TAPE's wow is faint (at most 0.25 %), no flutter; a change of delay time cross-fades instead of sliding; FILTER's drift is slow and narrow.
  • The engine's generation 1 (new sounds): IMPACT's pitch fall a thud of a few semitones, not a zap; BRUIT's sample-and-hold on the level more than the pitch; PULSE's pitch still; DRONE's vibrato faint; FORMANT and REED given an inharmonic modulator one time in two; a freeze never before the body's attack is over. Generation 0 is kept as it was (tests/golden).
  • The draw leans to the inharmonic: metals, bruits, impacts, glass, clouds, shatters, freezes up; formants and reeds down.
  • Latching: SHIFT + a white key latches its note on the chosen slot (the key stays lit while that slot is chosen); SHIFT + the key again lets it go. A latched note is never stolen while another can go. A new patch on a slot moves its held and latched notes over to the new sound instead of cutting them.
  • The screen: round each module, a border in the colours of the slots wired into it, shared out equally between them; the modules the chosen slot is wired into filled with its colour, their names white. How the modules are wired to each other is not drawn.

0.02 (2026-10-23): six slots and a rack

The owner's design after trying 0.01.

  • Six slots, a MOLECULE generator each, on the top row's six buttons: pressed, the slot chosen; held 0.8 s, the slot on, or off again. Only slot 1 is on at the start. The keys play the slot chosen; a key lifted ends its note on the slot it was played on. Six voices shared by the slots.
  • A rack of twelve modules, always there, in the signal's order: FILTER, FOLD, MULAW, SHIFT (a frequency shifter), MODAL, STRING, VOWEL, FLANGE, TAPE, REVERSE, SPRING, PLATE (rack.c, after docs/PROCESSORS.md). Where a module sits is where it sounds: the left column at the left, the right at the right. Each passes a guard (a level rider and a ceiling). MODAL and STRING are tuned to the scale's root.
  • A patch is a slot's: HOME draws the chosen slot's sound, its chain through one to three modules (in rack order: each feeds the next, the last goes out), its dry share, its level and pan, and now and then a modulation by another slot that is on (ring, amplitude, or a filter its level opens). SHIFT + HOME: a new one of the same family. HOME held 0.8 s: every slot that is on, anew. The draw follows Vascular's abstract path as 0.01's did. Modules fed by several slots hear their sum; a module's output goes to the next module of every chain through it, as a mult would. A module no slot feeds any more rings out where it went.
  • SEQ draws new values for the twelve modules (each at its home one time in five, else moved), keeping the wiring.
  • SELECT and ALGORITHM: the chosen slot's level and pan (said on the screen).
  • The screen: the load at the top left (red from 85 %), the battery at the top right, large; the six slots, a block each in its own colour (filled when on, an outline when off, white frame when chosen, brighter as it sounds, a corner square in the colour of the slot that modulates it); the rack as twelve named tiles, three across, lit as sound passes, a bar along each tile's foot in the colour of every slot wired into it, the chosen slot's chain framed in its colour. No cables. No family names.
  • Tests: host modules (every module alone, its level against the dry), the flows of the slots' buttons.

0.01 (2026-10-23): the first working version

The first installable build: a patch played from the keys.

  • The patch (patch.c): one generator (MOLECULE, mol.c) and a chain of up to four processors, drawn whole by HOME after Vascular's abstract path: a scene (FIELD, MATERIAL, FEEDBACK, EROSION) leans the generator's family and the chain's kinds; a harshness budget of 0, 1 or 2 pays for the rough families and the destructive or resonant kinds; a chain never has two kinds of one character nor two destructive ones; the reverb comes last, added as a shared tail by the scene's chance. The generator's place on the screen is its pan (across) and its level (down, the top loudest).
  • The processors (nodes.c): FILTER, CRUSH, DRIVE, FOLD, RING, COMB, FLANGE, DELAY, REVERB — Tonitor's filter, crush, distortion, delay and plate, and four after Vascular's (docs/PROCESSORS.md).
  • Six voices of the one generator, drawn from a pool as the notes need them; a stolen voice fades, a patch change fades them all; a released voice ends 66 dB under its loudest, or at 30 s.
  • The panel: HOME a new patch; the white keys play it in the scale chosen; ARP the SCALE page (Tonitor's 23 scales: SELECT the scale, ALGORITHM the root); OCT- and OCT+ the octave; MASTER the level; USB MIDI notes as the keys. SAVE and SEQ are kept for the sessions and the patterns; PLAY, REC and the top row do nothing yet.
  • The screen: the family's name, large, in its colour; the network — the generator a disc where the patch put it, the processors as rings on the way to the output, joined by lines; the chain's names along the bottom; the octave at the top right; the audio's load, small, at the bottom right (a diagnostic, for now).
  • The board layer: Tonitor's HAL, boot, USB (identity "FM-1 Molecular", PID 0x0007), the installer's handshake, the update loader and the rescue mode. One core renders; USB audio out, the TRS MIDI jack, sessions, the second core and the backup protocol are not in this build.
  • The host harness: the engine's checks, and now the firmware's — patches drawn and played through the real mixer, the flows (HOME under held notes, every key at once, forty patches in a row), the screens as PNG.

0.00 (2026-10-23): the engine stage

MOLECULE: six-operator FM (msfa in Felucca's integer port as Tonitor shaped it) with waves in its operators (28 band-limited single cycles, morph, phase distortion, the bend following the envelope) and a grain cloud after them (CLOUD, PULSAR, FREEZE). Twelve families on three paths, four macros, every sound measured to one level; the host harness and the golden hashes of generation 0.
